title: Derived completeness of the derived limit of a system killed by powers of the elements of an ideal
author: The Stacks Project Authors
work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra)
source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
difficulty_reason: The statement takes a ring A, an ideal I and an inverse system of objects K_n of D(A) on which every element f of I acts nilpotently in the sense that some power of f is zero on K_n, and asserts that for every K the derived limit of the objects K tensor^L K_n is derived complete with respect to I (statement lines 26287-26294). The proof proceeds by reducing along the two structural facts of the theory: derived complete objects are closed under derived limits, so the limit may be replaced by its terms, and the vanishing of the torsion functor is the criterion for derived completeness, so the nilpotence assumption on K_n gives the result term by term after tensoring with K (proof lines 26296-26301). The argument is short but complete, and it is the concatenation of the two reductions that makes the statement work with no finiteness hypothesis on K. The counted span is self-contained: it refers to no labelled item of the chapter and cites nothing.
